title: An empty column says 'Drag a work order here' only to users who can reassign
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard" and "Jenny Wilson"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-702 led by Esther Howard, nothing led by Jenny Wilson, no work order without a lead):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose the customer "ZZAUTOTEST Empty Columns" (add it with the Add button in the customer box if it does not exist; using it keeps this test's work orders apart from others at the location) and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
  6. Create a second user who can view but not change work orders:
    • Settings > Roles & Permissions > Create custom role (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST WO view only") > turn on Work Orders view, leave Work Orders create and edit off > Save.
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member with an email you can open (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Viewer"), role = the new role, enrolled at this location > Save, then accept the invitation and set a password.
    • Keep this user signed in in a second browser (or a private window) so you can switch between the two users.
custom_steps:
1. As your user (create and edit), open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST Empty Columns so only this test's work orders show.
  4. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  5. Read Jenny Wilson's empty column and the empty Unassigned column.
  6. In the second browser, as the view-only user, open Work Orders.
  7. Click the All tab.
  8. Click Search and type ZZAUTOTEST Empty Columns so only this test's work orders show.
  9. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  10. Read the same two columns.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • For your user, Jenny Wilson's column and the Unassigned column each show "Drag a work order here to assign it".
  • For the view-only user, the same two columns each show "No work orders".
  • The design shows "No work orders assigned" above "Drag a work order here to assign it" for everyone: extra or different wording is a fail, write down what you see.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S3-R20, read 8 Oct 2026. PO decision Chris Ward, PRD footer comment 6 Oct 2026 item 5. Design: Claude Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html), Board empty column; on-screen labels only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R20: “A technician column with no work orders under the current filters, and an empty Unassigned column, show “Drag a work order here to assign it” to a user who can reassign work orders (S4-N1), and “No work orders” to everyone else.”
